articles.headline: The Botanist and the Translator is a planet-wide plant mystery puzzle game published by Team Cherry and made by Hollow Knight: Silksong's own Hornet
keyFacts: Team Cherry announced The Botanist and the Translator, a hand-drawn puzzle game developed by voice actor Makoto Koji.
Players control Hatti and Oliver as they investigate a pollen-covered alien planet by sketching flora and translating critters.
The game has no release date yet, and players can currently wishlist it on Steam.
body: It's been a little over a year since Hollow Knight: Silksong launched after an eon of comments on Nintendo Directs asking "SILKSONG???", and now yesterday brought us the news that its first expansion, Sea of Sorrow, is due out next month. And it's free? Well ain't that lovely! Truth be told, however, I was actually a little more interested in everything that preceded the Sea of Sorrow trailer in yesterday's Cherry Time presentation. Namely, The Botanist and the Translator, a ridiculously delightful looking, hand-drawn game about solving a plant related mystery across an alien planet that is being developed by Makoto Koji, the voice actor behind Silksong's Hornet.

In The Botanist and the Translator, you play as Hatti, the titular botanist, alongside Oliver, her equally titular translator who is also a lightly Very Hungry Caterpillar-esque bug. They've been brought to a planet that's been covered in a "thick, sticky pollen," and it's up to them to figure out why all the plants are behaving so strangely. On the one side, as Hatti, you'll be sketching all the various flora you come across, as well as trying to figure out how they all work in point-and-click style puzzle minigames.

On the other side, with Oliver, you speak to all the numerous strange and charming critters across this planet, translating them for Hatti in a simple enough looking rhythm game that mixes things up depending on who's being spoken to. The visual identity on display here is really engrossing, in a short behind the scenes video shared by Team Cherry, Koji speaks of her origins as a children's book illustrator and you can really feel that here. You can get a sense of Team Cherry's influence in the gibberish voice acting too, it's very sweet!

Team Cherry are also publishing The Botanist and the Translator too, an initiative I'm glad to see they're taking given just how loaded they already were and surely once again are following the release of Silksong. There's no release date attached to this one just yet, so all we can do is hope that it doesn't take a Silksong amount of time. And in the meanwhile, we could always throw it a little wishlist on Steam.

articles.headline: Coach Pope booed off floor at Rupp as Wichita State shocks 4-3 Kentucky
keyFacts: Wichita State defeated Kentucky 73-71 in overtime for the program's first win against the Wildcats, dropping Kentucky to a 4-3 record.
Jordan Frison scored 20 points, while Dillon Battie and William Berg both recorded double-doubles to lead the Shockers to victory.
Coach Mark Pope stated that the team and coaching staff must improve following the home loss at Rupp Arena.
body: Jordan Frison came off the bench to score 20 points and Dillon Battie and William Berg posted double-doubles to lead Wichita State to a 73-71 overtime victory over struggling Kentucky in front of a disappointed crowd at Rupp Arena on Friday night.

Berg made two free throws and Michael Gray Jr. followed with a basket to knot the score at 65 with 51 seconds remaining. Mason Williams missed a jumper for the Wildcats, and Berg missed a shot at the buzzer to send the game to overtime.

The loss to the Shockers -- Wichita State's first triumph over Kentucky -- pushed the Wildcats to an uncharacteristic 4-3 on the season, and coach Mark Pope, a former Kentucky player, was sent off the floor with some boos after the overtime session.

"I do know this group. It's an incredibly resilient group, tough group, wants to be together and wants to compete," Pope said. "We clearly have areas where we need to get better, as players, and definitely as a coach. And so, we will."

Berg grabbed a rebound and scored to put the Shockers up 71-69 with 3:14 left in the extra period. Neither team scored again until Kentucky's Kam Williams snagged a rebound and scored to tie it at 71 with 65 seconds remaining.
Battie grabbed a miss and scored in the paint to put Wichita State up for good with 36 seconds left. Milan Momcilovic missed a 3-pointer on the game's final shot.

"It was a great environment. Grateful to [Big Blue Nation] for showing out," Pope said, referring to the crowd of 19,435 who witnessed the loss. "The gym was unbelievable, and our guys battled. We didn't play great, but they really fought. [It was] an unfortunate end to the game for us."

Frison made 6 of 14 shots with three 3-pointers and all five of his free throws for the Shockers (7-1), who beat Kentucky for the first time on their third try. Berg totaled 16 points and a career-high 20 rebounds, while Battie contributed 16 points and a career-high 17 boards. Gray scored 12 off the bench.
"A lot of it is on my shoulders," Pope said. "Congratulations to Wichita State, I thought they played really hard. They are a good team. They really competed and played well."
Reserves Mason Williams and Kam Williams both scored 16 to lead the Wildcats with Kam adding eight rebounds. Franck Kepnang and Momcilovic both scored 12.

Mason Williams, a freshman, had 10 points and Kepnang scored eight to help Kentucky take a 31-25 lead into halftime. Battie had 12 points for the Shockers, who fell behind by 14 before getting within two possessions at the break.
Kentucky has lost its last five overtime games dating to last season.

"It's the same always, whether we win or lose," Pope said, when asked what his message to the team was after the defeat. "Our job is to get up tomorrow and hit it as hard as we possibly can. If we won tonight by one, that would have been our job also."
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Full fight video: Chris Leben vs. Yoshihiro Akyiama run it back 16 years after UFC 116
keyFacts: Chris Leben defeated Yoshihiro Akiyama by split decision in an 89 kg bout at Black Combat 17 in Seoul, South Korea on Nov. 21.
Following the match, Akiyama tearfully announced his retirement from fighting and left his gloves at the center of the canvas.
Black Combat released the full video of the bout on Thursday, covering the walkouts through the backstage interviews.
body: The lights dimmed, and suddenly it felt a little like 2010 again as "Time to Say Goodbye" by Sarah Brightman and Andrea Bocelli echoed throughout Gocheok Sky Dome in Seoul, South Korea.

Yoshihiro Akiyama emerged from backstage, as over 21,000 fans cheered and chanted his name. Moments later, the mood swung. Chris Leben made his way to the cage, all business, sporting his bright red hair.
The 89 kg (~196 pounds) bout served as the co-main event for Black Combat 17 on Nov. 21.
Following the announcements, the fighters began to move around the cage, and it felt a little more like 2026.

Akiyama (16-8) is now 51 years old, and hadn't fought since a custom rules bout in January 2024. Leben (21-12) is 46, not having competed since a February 2021 bareknuckle boxing bout. The most recent MMA fight he had prior was his final UFC bout against Uriah Hall in December 2013.
Despite their ages and the potential for rust, the two UFC contenders of yesteryears went the distance. Leben defeated Akiyama by split decision (28-29, 28-29, 29-28).
After the fight, Akiyama tearfully announced his retirement. He laid his gloves down at center canvas and walked to the back as he received a full standing ovation.
On Thursday, Black Combat released a full version of the bout, from the walkouts through the backstage interviews. Check out that video above.

articles.headline: Argentina's bid to stop Falklands oil drilling rejected
keyFacts: An international tribunal rejected Argentina's bid to halt the Sea Lion oil exploration project near the Falkland Islands.
The tribunal ruled by a vote of 18-3 that it was the wrong court to decide on questions of territorial sovereignty.
Argentine President Javier Milei stated the ruling is not the final word, while UK officials called the decision a clear win.
body: - Published
Argentina's bid to block an oil exploration project near the Falkland Islands has been rejected by a UN-backed international tribunal.

The Argentinian government had called for the Sea Lion venture to be halted as it claimed there was an ongoing dispute over the sovereignty of the Falklands, a British overseas territory. The UK has repeatedly rejected that claim.
Speaking on Saturday, the president of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea said it was the wrong court to rule on questions of sovereignty. The decision was upheld in a vote 18-3.
After the ruling, Argentina's President Javier Milei said "this decision is not the final word" and declared "the Falkland Islands are Argentine".

Attorney General for England and Wales, Ellie Reeves, who presented the UK's legal arguments in Hamburg earlier this month, told the BBC the ruling was "really significant" and an "a clear win for the UK government".

Earlier, in a joint statement with Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, Reeves urged Argentina to "end its wider economic pressure" against the territory: "Argentina sought to stop the Falkland Islanders making their own sovereign decisions and failed in this attempt."
The case is the latest diplomatic row between the UK and Argentina, which fought a 74-day war over the islands in 1982.
The Sea Lion oilfield, around 130 miles (209 km) from the Falkland Islands, contains an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil.

Two oil companies â Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum â are due to begin extracting from the oilfield within two years, potentially generating huge revenues for the roughly 3,500 inhabitants of the islands.

But the Argentinian government claimed the marine environment of disputed maritime areas is protected by international law, arguing that while it believed there was a territorial dispute over the Falklands, nothing should be done that could change the situation - including the building of oil wells.

The UK responded that the Law of the Sea court had no jurisdiction over the issue, and that pausing the Sea Lion project could have huge economic consequences on the islands' local population and companies connected with the venture.
The tribunal's decision ultimately rested on its own powers - this was a territorial issue, and a maritime court was not the right place to hear the dispute.

Buenos Aires disagreed, writing in a statement after the decision that "Argentina did not ask the court to rule on sovereignty", but to apply the United Nations' sea laws to the UK over its "exploitation of our resources".

It also said that five individuals would face sanctions for their involvement in the oil drilling venture, something Milei had been threatening. The statement did not specify who the sanctions would be against.
"The message is clear: those who participate in the illegal exploitation of our resources will face the consequences," the statement said.
The 10-week war that was fought in 1982 started when Argentine forces landed on the Falklands to stake a territorial claim over the islands, as a British military task force fought to eject them.
The conflict led to the deaths of 255 British military personnel, three islanders and 649 Argentine military personnel.
Despite its defeat, Argentina has always maintained its right to the Falklands, and over the years, successive governments have pressed their claim with varying degrees of aggression and diplomacy.
The UK government has made clear that sovereignty remains with Britain and maintains that the island's population has a right to self-determination.
In a 2013 referendum, residents of the islands voted overwhelmingly to remain a British overseas territory - with 99.8% voting in favour and just three voting against.

articles.headline: Car speakers rattling? Try these fixes before calling a mechanic
keyFacts: Car speaker rattling is often caused by simple issues like high volume, power imbalances, debris, loose mounting hardware, or vibrating door panels rather than broken equipment.
Drivers can diagnose the problem by checking if the speaker is blown, testing different frequency ranges, and using visual or touch inspections.
Engadget reports that motorists can try do-it-yourself fixes like tightening mounting screws, adjusting amplifier gain, checking wiring, or adding sound-deadening materials before calling a mechanic.
body: Car speakers rattling? Try these fixes before calling a mechanic
Check these common culprits before you go to the pros.

There you are, just singing along to your favorite tunes when you hear that awful noise. Rattling car speakers. Your mind probably wanders right to your bank account balance, because this is definitely going to cost you hundreds, if not thousands, of dollars for a new car audio system. Right?

Not so fast. Rattling car speakers, while extremely annoying, may not be the result of any catastrophic audio equipment failure or damage. It could actually be a simple fix. So, before you take your car to an audio specialist and have a new sound system installed, try to first determine the cause of the rattling. Then see if one of these easy solutions works for you.
What may be causing your car speakers to rattle

Obviously, if components within the speakers are damaged, rattling can occur. But the culprits are often simply power and volume. If your speakers are using more power than the speaker cone can handle, the result is typically rattling and distortion. But not enough power, usually caused by a weak amplifier, can also cause distortion.

As far as volume is concerned, you probably already know that the higher the volume (especially if there's lots of bass), the more likely your car speakers are going to rattle. The reason? Science. Bass frequencies use a lot of power, and that causes more movement in the cones inside the speakers. That movement can cause loose components in the speaker to move against each other. Heavy bass also makes your car's door panels vibrate, in which case it may not be your speakers vibrating at all. But it's not just booming bass that can cause rattling issues. High volume creates excess heat in the speaker's voice coil, resulting in rattle-like distortion.

Debris finding its way into the speakers can also cause rattling if it comes into contact with moving speaker parts. And the cabinet that holds the speaker within the door panels or rear decks often vibrates with the music if the surfaces are poorly dampened — this creates a rattling sound that many people think is coming from the speakers themselves.

The rattling, especially if it occurs even at low volumes, could also be something as simple as loose mounting hardware. When the screws come loose, as a result of either poor installation or road vibration, rattling is common. Check to see if there is space between the speaker and its mounting surface. If so, tightening the screws should help. Also, try pressing the speaker panel when you hear distortion. If the distortion stops when you press it, it's likely just loose mounting hardware or noise from the cabinet.

With all these possibilities, the next thing to do is try to eliminate some of the causes and diagnose the origin of the rattling so you can determine whether it can be fixed at home or needs to be seen by a professional.
Is the speaker just rattling or is it blown?

The first thing to focus on is finding out whether the speaker is simply rattling or if it's completely blown. If it's just rattling, it should be fixable. If it's blown, however, you're going to need a new speaker.

You can often tell if a speaker is blown simply by listening. For example, you'll hear distortion at any volume level, where rattling typically only happens at high volumes. Another thing to listen for is a missing frequency, like a lack of bass or no high frequency. This could be the result of a broken speaker.

If you determine that the speaker is not blown, it's time to start testing different tones and frequency ranges to identify the source of the rattling. Using test tones or the equalizer on your stereo's head unit, try out different frequency ranges to find the point where the rattling occurs. Rattling coming from low frequencies signals that the problem may involve bass-related components like subwoofers (if your vehicle has them) or bass response. If the rattling occurs during midrange frequencies, the culprit could be the door speakers. And if you notice the rattling when high frequencies are played, it might be smaller components like the tweeters.

Finally, use the eye and touch tests. Thoroughly check your speaker for any broken components; surrounds, voice coils and cones are typically the components that show visual damage. And if any of them are broken or damaged, it's time for a new speaker.
Troubleshooting a rattling car speaker

First, check the speaker wiring, especially if you've ever had work done on the speakers or have done any yourself. Sometimes the rattling can simply be reversed polarity, with the positive and negative terminals incorrectly connected. More often, however, wiring can become jarred loose from years of road vibration. You can test this by playing music and then lightly wiggling the speaker wires behind the head unit or where they come into the door. If the noise stops or gets worse when you move the wire, it's either a loose terminal or a break in the wire's insulation.

If you've diagnosed a power issue, there are a few fixes to try. If overpowering is the problem, start by reducing the gain on your amplifier and then slowly increasing it until you find the right balance. A multimeter can come in handy here, as it'll let you know whether you're going beyond the speakers' RMS power rating. If underpowering is the problem, you can either upgrade the amplifier or disconnect some speakers to cut down on the amp's load.

Test out your equalizer settings by resetting your EQ to zero across the board, then play music and gradually turn up the settings until you identify where the rattling begins. If you can find the frequency range where the rattling starts, you should be able to adjust your settings until the rattling stops.

If you think loose mounting hardware is the cause of the rattling, take off the speaker grilles and check to see whether any mounting screws are loose. Any trouble tightening them may require longer screws or new mounting holes. To minimize vibrations, you can also add a foam gasket between the mounting surface and the speaker.

Adding sound-deadening material like peel-and-stick butyl rubber mats with an aluminum foil backing to some of the flat metal surfaces on your car's door panels can also minimize resonance. Closed-cell foam decoupling sheets, weather stripping tape or foam speaker baffle rings placed around the speaker and along the panel edges also act as a cushion between vibrating pieces.

Ultimately, if these fixes don't help, there could be major damage to a speaker component, at which point replacement by a car audio specialist probably makes the most sense. But it's definitely worth giving these DIY fixes a shot before you drop big money on new speakers.

articles.headline: This new sports app is designed specifically for women’s sports
keyFacts: A new app called Rival launched on iOS and Android to provide a community hub for women's sports fans without real-money gambling.
Founder Kelly DiPaola stated that the platform was created to offer a safe, harassment-free environment focusing on friendly competition and fan connections.
Rival currently covers 36 leagues and plans to expand its sports coverage, social features, and live-picks ecosystem in the future.
body: A new sports app is looking to change the way fans engage with women’s sports, and it’s doing so without the real-money gambling that has become increasingly common in the sports world.
Called Rival, the app officially launched last weekend on the App Store and Google Play Store, timed to coincide with the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) Championship.

With Rival, users can make free-to-play picks, earn points, compete on leaderboards, create and join groups, and connect with other fans. The platform also serves as a hub for discovering women’s sports, bringing together schedules, scores, news, highlights, and information on where to watch.

The app is the brainchild of Kelly DiPaola, whose previous experience includes working for Barbra Streisand and producing unscripted television, including Netflix’s “Selling Sunset.” The idea grew out of her frustration with traditional sports apps, which tend to prioritize scores and statistics over the fan experience. Rather than simply creating another place to check game results, DiPaola envisioned a destination dedicated to women’s sports, where fans could build connections, find community, and feel more invested in the games they follow.

“I’m a passionate sports fan, and my partner, Jodie Taylor, is a former England Lioness and now Technical Director at Arsenal Women,” DiPaola told TechCrunch in an email. “The original spark was my frustration with the disparity in women’s sports coverage on traditional sports betting platforms. I’ve never been particularly good at accepting inequality as the status quo, so I decided to do something about it.”

That vision comes at a time when women’s sports are experiencing record growth in attendance and viewership. Yet greater visibility doesn’t necessarily translate into a better experience for fans, particularly women who participate in mainstream sports communities online.
Platforms such as Reddit, X, and sports-focused forums can expose women — especially women of color and LGBTQ+ athletes — to harassment, abuse, and discriminatory commentary.

The problem is well documented. A 2024 NCAA study found that online abuse targeting student-athletes peaked during March Madness, with women’s basketball players receiving three times as many threats as their male counterparts.

Rival is positioning itself as an alternative to that experience, placing positive social connection and community at the center of its platform. Users can create profiles and statuses, follow other users, and create or join groups around their favorite teams and sports.

“Women’s sports doesn’t just have a visibility problem. It has a participation problem,” DiPaola said. “I wanted to build somewhere that felt like walking into your favorite local bar on a Friday night, where you could turn up on your own and still feel like you belonged, like you were part of something bigger than yourself.”

Although the app is focused on women’s teams and competitions, anyone can join. The platform also includes blocking and reporting tools, private profiles, private groups, in-app support, and moderation features designed to address abusive behavior.

“Our responsibility is to create a safe and welcoming environment for everyone,” DiPaola said. “We have zero tolerance for abuse, harassment, or discrimination, and accounts engaging in such behavior are subject to removal. As our community grows, our moderation capabilities will need to grow with it.”

Another major differentiator is Rival’s decision to avoid real-money sports betting altogether. Instead, the platform centers on what the company describes as “friendly competition,” allowing users to make predictions and compete with friends without putting money on the line.

That distinction is particularly timely as sports betting continues to expand across the U.S., raising concerns about its consequences. According to the American Gaming Association, Americans wagered $166.94 billion on legal sports betting last year. A UCLA study found that, in states allowing online sports gambling, the likelihood of a personal bankruptcy filing increased by around 25%.

At launch, Rival covers 36 leagues and competitions, 1,979 teams, and more than 20,000 athletes internationally. This includes NCAA Women’s Basketball, NCAA Softball, Women’s Professional Football League, EuroLeague, and more.

DiPaola says the company ultimately wants to represent every sport women play, including those that have historically received less coverage. That will mean exploring partnerships to improve data availability for underrepresented sports and leagues.

Looking ahead, Rival also plans to expand its sports coverage, develop its live-picks ecosystem, introduce “richer” social and community features, and bring fan participation closer to live broadcasts.

articles.headline: Blue Jays are 'ideal landing spot' for Cubs 26-HR free agent despite Jazz Chisholm Jr.
keyFacts: Andy McCullough of The Athletic named the Toronto Blue Jays as the ideal landing spot for free-agent Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki.
The Blue Jays have money to spend and need outfield help, making Suzuki a strong fit after a 2026 season where he hit 26 home runs.
Suzuki is likely to seek a 120 million dollar deal, and the Blue Jays could potentially add him alongside their recent acquisition Jazz Chisholm Jr.
body: The Toronto Blue Jays missed out on Tarik Skubal, and they missed out on Teruaki Sato this offseason. But they've already begun to pivot, landing Kaima Taira and Jazz Chisholm Jr.

While those are two notable additions, the Blue Jays might not be close to being done. They offered Skubal $400 million, and the Taira and Chisholm deals aren't even close to half their offer to Skubal. So, it shouldn't be a surprise if they get involved elsewhere.

Andy McCullough of The Athletic named the Blue Jays as the "ideal landing spot" for free-agent Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki. Even after landing Chisholm, the Blue Jays would be a great landing spot for Suzuki this offseason.
Seiya Suzuki's 'ideal' landing spot is with Blue Jays
"The Blue Jays have money to spend and a zeal to spend it," McCullough writes. "... The team needs more outfield help, and Suzuki has been a steady performer since arriving in America in 2022."

Chisholm will help out the Blue Jays' infield, but this team could use help in the outfield. Jonatan Clase, Brett Bateman and Nathan Lukes could all start for the Blue Jays in the outfield next season.

While there is some appeal to all three, adding an elite hitter like Suzuki, who has the ability to hit 26 home runs and also control the strike zone, would be an incredible pickup for the Blue Jays this offseason.
Suzuki might be a little bit older, at 32 years old; he's coming off a strong 2026 season in which he had a .270 batting average with 26 homers, 5.1 bWAR, and elite defense in the outfield.
With the Cubs landing Sato this offseason, it would seem Suzuki might not return to the Cubs this offseason, especially with Suzuki likely to seek a $120 million deal like what Sato got.

It might be a lot of money for the Blue Jays to spend on Suzuki, but with their willingness to spend big this offseason, overpaying a little bit to guarantee they land Suzuki, arguably the best bat available this offseason, would make a lot of sense.

Being able to add both Suzuki and Chisholm in one offseason would be quite the haul for the Blue Jays. Chisholm's deal wasn't too expensive, so a big Suzuki contract wouldn't hurt as bad if they land the Cubs star outfielder.

articles.headline: GTA 6's Long Development Cycle Even Made Rockstar Question If It Would Ever Launch
keyFacts: Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson revealed that some staff doubted Grand Theft Auto 6 would ever launch during its 13-year development.
Nelson said the long development cycle included finishing Red Dead Redemption 2 before 2018 and multiple delays after the 2022 reveal.
Despite the stress of the lengthy production, Grand Theft Auto 6 has successfully released and broken sales records.
body: While Grand Theft Auto 6 is real, out now, and breaking all sorts of records with how well it's selling, it felt like the game might never be released at some points during its lengthy 13-year development. In a recent interview, Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson revealed that even those within Rockstar sometimes felt that way about GTA 6.
"A lot of us felt like the day would never come"

Nelson, who was one of the lead developers on GTA 6, shared this sentiment in an interview with GamesRadar ahead of the game's release, saying that "it feels surreal" for the highly anticipated game to finally be out. He was also blunt that some people at Rockstar weren't sure the Nov. 19 launch of GTA 6 would ever happen because of how long it took to develop.

"I think a lot of us felt like the day would never come," he explained. "A lot of us, certainly on the senior team, have shipped a fair few games. But it's been a while since we've done one of these and this one took a good chunk of time to sort of figure it out.I think it's surreal, it's a relief – we're very nervous, when you get really close to something maybe your perspective is a little bit compromised. But yeah, we're in a little bit of disbelief and we probably will be until release, and then hopefully it'll become real once people are talking about it and playing it."

A 13-year development cycle is certainly unusual in the video game industry, but GTA 6 was anything but your usual AAA game. It was a sequel to one of the best-selling games of all time and had a scope far greater than most open-world games. The game's development was also elongated, as Rockstar had to focus on finishing Red Dead Redemption 2 before 2018 and then made the tough decision to delay GTA 6 a couple of times after it was officially revealed in 2022.

The wait and long development cycle seem worth it in the end, as GTA 6 has been a massive success. Still, Nelson's comments show that even those at Rockstar felt the pressure and stress that comes with working on such a highly anticipated game for so long.

articles.headline: Albania: Clashes erupt at anti-government protest in Tirana
keyFacts: Clashes erupted between police and protesters in Tirana on Saturday as thousands demanded the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama.
Demonstrators cited corruption, poverty, and living conditions, while Prime Minister Rama's government denied corruption allegations and called for dialogue.
Rama's government introduced measures such as cheaper fuel and financial support for low-income families to ease public discontent.
body: Clashes broke out between police and protesters in Albania's capital, Tirana, on Saturday as thousands of people demanded the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama.
The demonstration began peacefully but groups of masked protesters later broke away from the march and attacked government buildings with stones and petrol bombs.

Police responded with tear gas, water cannons and rubber bullets. Protesters also used wooden sticks to try to smash street cameras and windows at ministry buildings, while clouds of tear gas spread through several streets in the city center.

People traveled to Tirana from across Albania and abroad to join the rally, which coincided with the 114th anniversary of the country's declaration of independence. The day is usually marked by celebrations and is a public holiday. Police set up checkpoints on major roads leading into and out of the capital.
"I came here specifically for the protest," 33-year-old Arian Lleshi, who traveled from the United Kingdom told AFP news agency.

"Why? Because we have been suffering for far too long. We have spread ourselves across Europe and around the world and it is almost as if we are citizens without a state. We are like stateless citizens," he said.

Lleshi said political parties that have dominated Albania since the fall of communism in the 1990s no longer represented the population. He called for a new generation of intellectuals and people more invested in the country's future to take their place.
Protests against Edi Rama have widened

Saturday's demonstration was part of a series of protests that began in late May, initially triggered by opposition to a major luxury tourism development on Albania's southern coast. The project is linked to an investment firm founded by Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump.

The protests, known as the Flamingo movement, were followed by student demonstrations in September. Students called for improvements in education and living standards, with some rallies turning violent.

Demonstrations have since spread to other cities, fuelled by anger over alleged government corruption, unemployment and poor public services. Protesters have also called for better access to healthcare and an improvement in living conditions.
The demands have broadened to include calls for Edi Rama's resignation. Demonstrators gathered in Tirana's main Skanderbeg Square, chanting slogans demanding he step down.
"We have come out to demand our rights. We have had enough. Life has become very difficult. We are calling for a change to the entire system," student Juna Vasili told AP news agency.
Retiree Suzana Gjeta said she was protesting on behalf of both young people and pensioners struggling with low incomes.
"We are living on just 120 euros a month. We hope this system will go, that Edi Rama will go, and that this corruption will end," she told AP.
45-year-old engineer Eralda Baze also joined Saturday's rally. "Enough is enough; the corruption, the poverty, the immigration," she told Reuters.
Government denies corruption allegations

Rama's government has denied corruption allegations and called for dialogue with protesters. It has also introduced measures including cheaper fuel and additional financial support for low-income families in an attempt to ease public discontent.
Rama has been in power since 2013 and secured a fourth consecutive term in last year's parliamentary elections. His government has set a target of bringing Albania into the European Union by 2030.

Corruption scandals have repeatedly raised concerns about governance in Albania. Analysts have also described the country as a hub for criminal networks seeking to launder money from drug and weapons trafficking.

Rama has said his government is tackling corruption more vigorously than previous administrations. He has also defended the proposed coastal tourism development, saying it is legal and that natural habitats would be protected.

articles.headline: Farrell says low Twickenham crowd for Ireland win 'a shame'
keyFacts: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell described the low crowd of 32,000 for his teams victory over Australia at Twickenham as a shame.
Farrell questioned the Friday night timing and venue choice for the match, stating that the tournament format does not make sense.
Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney said organisers are pleased with the inaugural tournament despite admitting tweaks are needed.
body: - Published
Ireland head coach Andy Farrell said it was a "shame" his side's Nations Championship victory over Australia was played in front of a low crowd at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium.
Friday night's fifth-place play-off attracted an attendance of just 32,000 with the uppermost tier of the 82,000-capacity stadium entirely closed.
Ireland beat the Wallabies 38-14 after Italy overcame Fiji on the first day of the inaugural competition's finals day weekend at the home of England rugby.

Ticket sales for Saturday and Sunday's action, which are headlined by England v New Zealand and the final between South Africa and France, have been stronger, but Farrell questioned the Friday night double-bill.
"I'd love to spend some time to have a think about it, I've been preparing a team and you're busy doing that," he said.
"But off the top of my head, I don't know whether the Friday night thing works or being at the same venue. If we'd have played at the Aviva (Stadium in Dublin), it would have been full.

"They look like little things, but they're not, they mean a lot to the fans, like when you don't know where your team's playing and then you're trying to get a flight and all of a sudden they're Â£1,700. It doesn't fit."
Format 'doesn't make sense'
Farrell said he enjoyed parts of the spectacle, which included a pre-game performance from British popstar Myles Smith.
"I love what they're trying to do. I love the razzmatazz and coming into the ground it felt different. It felt like it was trying to be like an event, like a concert," he added.
"It was just a shame that we couldn't get the people through the door. The pre-match hype looked fantastic on the TV â from what I saw in the dressing room anyway.
"The 16:40 game â I felt for those boys really. And Sam Prendergast didn't get anything for man of the match, so playing for fifth place obviously didn't mean much."

Ireland won five of their six pool games to finish third in the northern hemisphere table behind France and England, while Australia finished third in the southern hemisphere standings behind South Africa and New Zealand after losing four matches.
"It's strange, it doesn't make sense," Farrell said.
"But it's not our jobs to make sense of it. It's our job to just keep playing what's in front of our faces."

While Farrell was left unconvinced by parts of the finals weekend, Rugby Football Union (RFU) chief executive Bill Sweeney said organisers are pleased with the first edition of the competition while admitting "tweaks" are needed in the future.
"We knew Friday was going to be a tough sell," Sweeney told ITV.

"I think we had just over 30 (thousand) here last night but when you consider we've sold over 160,000 tickets over three days for an inaugural tournament where a lot of us bought blind when frankly people didn't know what the match-ups were going to be, we're really pleased with that.
"When you look at the TV viewership, we should get over 100 million people watching this, so that's 170% up on where we were with the autumns, so we're really happy."

articles.headline: Mexico files complaint over DEA tip lines for reporting cartel members and corrupt officials
keyFacts: Mexico filed a formal complaint with the United States regarding new DEA tip lines intended for reporting cartel members and corrupt officials.
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum stated that the bilateral relationship involves coordination rather than subordination and criticized the U.S. for shifting responsibility.
The complaint followed the arrest of cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Sinaloa, with Mexico planning to try him before considering extradition.
body: Mexico filed a formal complaint with the United States over the Drug Enforcement Administration’s new tip lines for reporting cartel members or corrupt government officials.
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum unveiled the action on Friday while delivering her daily morning briefing.
“We have made it very clear in our relationship with the United States that the relationship is one of coordination, not subordination,” Sheinbaum said.

On Wednesday, DEA Administrator Terry Cole announced the agency set up dedicated tip lines for receiving information about members and associates of foreign terrorist organizations, corrupt government officials providing material support to designated FTOs, and criminal networks and individuals laundering money to finance narcoterrorism.
Sheinbaum argued the announcement gives the impression that Mexico is solely responsible for cracking down on drug use and cartel activity within the U.S.

“The United States has a responsibility to its people to address drug use, as well as to arrest members of the drug cartels operating in the United States,” she said. “We cannot have this view that the responsibility lies with Mexico.”
MEXICO CAPTURES CARTEL LEADER LISTED AS ONE OF TOP 10 MOST WANTED IN US

The complaint came nearly a week after Mexican special forces arrested Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, also known as “El Chapo Isidro,” in the northern state of Sinaloa with the help of U.S. intelligence. The U.S. government offered up to $5 million for information leading to his arrest.
Meza Flores was on the FBI’s top 10 most wanted list, signifying the importance of his capture. The U.S. put in a request for his extradition, but Mexico is moving forward with trying him first.

articles.headline: GOP lawmaker who defied blue wave reveals roadmap to win back Gen Z
keyFacts: Rep. Clay Fuller told Fox News Digital that Republicans need to focus on economic issues and housing affordability to win back young voters.
Fuller said that high housing costs and the average age of first-time homebuyers being 39 are major hurdles for Gen Z.
Fuller stated that over the next two years, the GOP must implement pro-economic and individual rights policies to prove they can restore the American dream.
body: Rep. Clay Fuller, R-Ga., said he knows how to get young voters back into the GOP fold.

"Since Charlie Kirk's assassination, I think our side has kind of completely lost the ability to talk to younger Americans," Fuller, who took over for Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, R-Ga., told Fox News Digital.

"I think when we talk to younger Americans, I want to talk directly to that young man or young woman who only has the ability to live in their parents' home because they can't afford a house. Do you know what the average age of a first-time homebuyer in the United States is? It's 39. And that shouldn't be where we are as a country."

At 45 years old, Fuller skews on the younger end of Congress. He's also one of the relatively few bright spots Republicans have seen since November — Fuller won his first full term on Nov. 3 by nearly 20 points, while the House GOP overall suffered significant losses.
BILLIONS SPENT BY KEY FEDERAL AGENCY HASN'T MADE AMERICAN DREAM OF HOMEOWNERSHIP ANY EASIER: REPORT
Fuller first came to Congress in mid-2026 via a special election when Greene abruptly resigned amid a public falling out with President Donald Trump .
FLORIDA CONGRESSMAN DIAGNOSES GOP'S BLUE TSUNAMI LOSSES: 'WE FAILED TO MAKE THEM THINK WE CARED ABOUT THEM'
And unlike his predecessor toward the end, Fuller has not created divisions between himself and his fellow Republicans. But he's calling on them to do more for America's youth.

He lamented the "brain drain" plaguing both his northwest Georgia district and other parts of the U.S. far outside major cities. Young people leave after college to seek out urban centers with more opportunity, creating a seemingly neverending cycle that sees economic downturns drain the life out of small American communities.
I'M GEN Z: IF THE GOP WANTS MY VOTE, STOP THE SPEECHES AND FIX THE HOUSING CRISIS

"That's the number one thing that I'm focused on every day, is making sure that we're bringing that American dream back to being a reality," Fuller said. "I want that to be true for young Americans, too. When they look at the town that they grew up in and their ancestors have been buried in, they know that they can stay there and have a career."
Fuller himself built a career in his home state, serving in the military after graduating from college before working as a district attorney in northwest Georgia.

He said Republicans could have the high ground with young Americans if they doubled down on their economic policies, as well as the "larger philosophical outlook about who we are as a country and individual rights."

"I want to talk to those young Americans to say, 'Look, I know this isn't your first choice of where you want to be. And you're doing everything you can to achieve that American dream. That white picket fence should be a reality to you, and every policy that we should put in place, from immigration to economic policy to national security, should be focused on making sure that dream is more accessible to you than it was a couple of weeks ago,'" Fuller said.

"We just have to double down on supporting those policies and putting them in place and keeping that promise to the American voter, and they'll turn back, especially once they see how crazy some of the people that got elected to the House and Senate are going to be."

Young voters were among the key groups who turned away from the GOP en masse during the last election. Fox News' Power Rankings cited disenchantment with the Iran war and Trump's tariffs as key reasons for many Americans' rejection of the right.
JUSTIN HASKINS: 3 HUGE REASONS REPUBLICANS LOST. HERE’S WHAT THEY NEED TO WIN IN 2028
Fuller argued that the next two years, however, will demonstrate that Democrats' policies are not conducive to bringing the American dream back to reality.

"They know what was available to their great-grandparents and their grandparents. That's all they want to see," Fuller said. "I think we can put those economic policies in place, and those young Americans that felt like a house is too far out of reach ... we can put the economic policies in place that makes that a reality. And I think at that point, yeah, people will support us because they know that socialism and communism, it doesn't work."

During his lengthy sitdown with Fox News Digital, Fuller maintained a focus on economic and health issues for his district — citing "forever chemical" like PFAS multiple times and his push to combat the high rates of cancer among his constituents — even when asked about his predecessor's penchant for throwing verbal bombs at both Democrats and fellow Republicans.
He said he had no ill will toward Greene and even lauded her dedicated staff.

"I certainly had talked to her. There were people in our office who had been long-term staff members of hers and appreciated her opinion on both the district and the staff that we had, especially in our district office," Fuller said when asked if Greene helped him with the transition. "She talked glowingly about everybody that worked there, and we have an incredible in-district team. But otherwise, again, I always know any position that I'm going to add to, I've got my own priorities, I've got my own focus. And from day one, that's what I've been focused on."

articles.headline: GTA 6 has successfully done what only one other game has ever managed: a good nightclub
keyFacts: PC Gamer reported that Grand Theft Auto 6 features realistic and immersive open-world nightclubs that rival the Berlin level in Hitman 3.
The reviewer stated that Vice City's three main clubs offer distinct atmospheres, ranging from luxury venues to underground raves.
The reviewer noted that the game captures realistic details, including dense crowds, detailed interiors, and patrons gathered outside smoking or queueing.
body: When Hitman 3 first launched in 2021, it was the first time since Absolution that I'd felt a strong urge to step into the shoes of Agent 47. The reason: its Berlin level. Set in the grimy, sweaty Club Hölle, it was the first time I'd ever seen a videogame get a nightclub right. The density of people on the dancefloor, the slight griminess that coated the whole place. The lights, the music. I didn't think another game would out-do it anytime soon.
And then Grand Theft Auto 6 happened.

There's an awful lot to be impressed with in Rockstar's newest blockbuster—and I should hope so, considering how much money and time went into making the damn thing—but nothing has stood out to me more than Leonida's nightlife. Hitman 3 did it excellently in isolation, but GTA 6 has managed to incorporate an immersive, lively club scene right into the open world.

And after spending far too much time in Vice City's Big Three—that's NINE1NINE, Jack of Hearts, and The Vault—I'm floored not only by how good a job Rockstar did of making them feel like a club you would end up inside in real life, but how distinct they all are from one another.

You've got your overpriced luxury half-strip-club, half-regular-club with NINE1NINE (inspired by Miami's own E11EVEN), where a beer costs 15 goddamn bucks even after you already fork out the $150 cover charge to get in. There's the sticky, dollar bill-laden floors of Jack of Hearts where MCs belt out over the mic and the bass practically splits the speakers open. And then you've got the cool, underground rave vibes of The Vault with multiple floors offering different music styles.

Even before heading inside each one, its patrons spill out of the doors and onto the sidewalks. Some are queueing up waiting to get in, while others huddle around back entrances having a smoke and talking about all the diabolical topics you get into after a few drinks. They aren't just isolated interiors, capturing the parts of the night that happen outside of the club itself.
Evacuate the dancefloor

That's an issue videogame nightclubs so often have: its people. A smattering of NPCs here and there, standing idly around in a venue that's a little too well-lit and making me feel like I just rocked up at 2 pm on a Monday afternoon.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Yet everywhere you look in GTA 6's nightclubs, you'll find swarms of bodies. The Vault is by far my favourite nightclub of the three—perhaps because it's the closest to what I've experienced in the real world—and as I walked around it shocked me just how carefully placed every single person felt.

The dancefloor is densely packed and I have to weave through sweaty bodies to make my way to the front. That's already impressive enough in itself. But it's also the punters who clutter the stairways; some sat on a step alone as they scroll through their phone, others gathered in clusters in an attempt to converse away from the noise and throng of drunken ravers. I've seen those people countless times in my own real-life nighttime excursions. Hell, I've been those people.

Sure, these people are ultimately set pieces, rarely (if ever) moving from their carefully curated posts. Dancers might wander around and bartenders will walk up and down serving drinks, leaving the rest of its people surprisingly static. But in the grand scheme of things, it doesn't matter. How often are you paying attention to what everyone else is up to in a nightclub, anyway?

Even the ways these things are decorated, man. Seeing half-drunk beer bottles perched atop ATM machines and drink cups cluttering up the bar makes me feel like people have actually been here and lived their life. There are so many small details that have gone into making each place feel like somewhere you've been in the real world, and that's even without me mentioning all the extra little ways Sony's DualSense controller amps up the experience.

I'm not sure how long it'll be until we get nightclubs that feel this damn good again. They feel like venues put together by people who've stayed out dancing until the lights come on at 3 am, only filtered out onto the streets by harsh fluorescents and the sudden absence of music. From the music choices, to the strobed lights and fog machines, to those utterly wild conversations you'd only be privy to in the smoking area, Rockstar has managed to curate the best nightlife going.

Mollie spent her early childhood deeply invested in games like Killer Instinct, Toontown and Audition Online, which continue to form the pillars of her personality today. She joined PC Gamer in 2020 as a news writer and now lends her expertise to write a wealth of features, guides and reviews with a dash of chaos. She can often be found causing mischief in Final Fantasy 14, using those experiences to write neat things about her favourite MMO. When she's not staring at her bunny girl she can be found sweating out rhythm games, pretending to be good at fighting games or spending far too much money at her local arcade.

articles.headline: How To Unlock More Hair And Makeup For Jason And Lucia In GTA 6 – Magazine Styles Guide
keyFacts: Players can unlock additional hair and makeup options for Jason and Lucia in Grand Theft Auto 6 by collecting specific magazine styles scattered across counties like Mariana, Kelly, Leonard, and Vice-Dale.
The collectible magazines are hidden in various locations, including residential homes, motel poolsides, rooftops, and commercial buildings throughout the game world.
Gathering all the magazine styles gives players expanded customization choices for altering the appearances of the two main characters.
body: Jason and Lucia are often on the run in Grand Theft Auto 6 , but that doesn’t mean they can’t pull a Mangione and look good while they’re at it. Yes, your characters can be dashing and glamorous as they rise to the top of the criminal underworld. However, you still need to gather collectibles--Jason Magazine Styles and Lucia Magazine Styles--if you wish to unlock more options for their hair and makeup.
In This Article
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Mariana County Jason Magazine Style #1: Square Goatee (Facial Hair)
Jason Magazine Style #2: Red-braided Cornrows Topknot (Hairstyle)
Lucia Magazine Style #1: Sunset Blush (Makeup)

Jason Magazine Style #3: Mutton Chops (Hairstyle)
Jason Magazine Style #4: Cowboy Horseshoe Mustache (Facial Hair)
Lucia Magazine Style #3: High Bun and MyMy Clip (Hairstyle)
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Kelly County Lucia Magazine Style #1: Lilac Brown 90s Beachy Waves (Hairstyle)
Lucia Magazine Style #2: Smoky Blue (Makeup)
Jason Magazine Style #1: Platinum Undercut Mullet (Hairstyle)
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Leonard County Magazine Style #1: Diamond-Adorned Pink Cat Eye (Makeup)
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Vice-Dale County: South Lucia Magazine Style #1: Ear Web Buzz Cut (Hairstyle)
Lucia: Magazine Style #2: Gothic Garnet (Makeup)
Jason Magazine Style #1: Green & Red Shards Buzz Cut (Hairstyle)
Jason Magazine Style #2: Light Blonde Wavy Spikes (Hairstyle)
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Vice-Dale County: West Jason Magazine Style #3: Hipster Mustache (Facial Hair)
Jason Magazine Style #4: Rose Buzz Cut (Hairstyle)
Jason Magazine Style #5: Lumberjack (Facial Hair)
Lucia Magazine Style #3: 80s Pop Shimmer (Makeup)
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Vice-Dale County: North Lucia Magazine Style #4: Rose High Twin Buns (Hairstyle)
Lucia Magazine Style #5: Tiger Eyes (Makeup)
Lucia Magazine Style #6: Floral Bun & Wavy Framing (Hairstyle)
Jason Magazine Style #6: Van Dyke (Facial Hair)
Jason Magazine Style #7: Rainbow Leopard Buzz Cut (Hairstyle)
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Vice-Dale County: East Jason Magazine Style #8:Blonde-Brown Side Part Curtains (Hairstyle)
Lucia Magazine Style #7: Orange-Purple Neon Cat Eye (Makeup)
Lucia Magazine Style #8: Spiky Bun & Framing (Hairstyle)

Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Mariana County
There are several GTA 6 Magazine Styles for Jason and Lucia in Mariana County, the first major zone in the campaign.
Jason Magazine Style #1: Square Goatee (Facial Hair)
Found inside a small wooden home just across the Rusty Anchor. The magazine is on a bed.
Jason Magazine Style #2: Red-braided Cornrows Topknot (Hairstyle)
Go to Dolphin Drive in the northeastern part of Key Lento and look for an octagon-shaped house. Climb up the steps to the left and check the rooftop patio.
Lucia Magazine Style #1: Sunset Blush (Makeup)
This GTA 6 Lucia Magazine Style is inside a house along Sunset Drive. It’s just a short distance away from Donnie’s trailer.
Lucia Magazine Style #2: Pop Star (Makeup)

Head to the Abismo Key State Park in the southern part of Mariana County. Go to the back of the building--i.e. the side facing the sea and check the ground in front of the door with the “Staff Only” sign.
Jason Magazine Style #3: Mutton Chops (Hairstyle)
Go to Sweetbay Road in Watson Bay and look for the Plaza Island Motel. The item is on a table to the right of the reception area.
Jason Magazine Style #4: Cowboy Horseshoe Mustache (Facial Hair)

From the above collectible, make your way across the bridge to Kingston Road (which is fairly close to the Unidentified Animal Pen WAiNK Curiosity ). Go to the house shown in the image above and check the chair in the bedroom.
Lucia Magazine Style #3: High Bun and MyMy Clip (Hairstyle)

This Lucia Style Magazine is in a mansion along Coconut Cove Court in the northwestern part of Capri. Inside the manor, you’ll find a luxury watch, a collectible card, and this magazine, which is on a lounge chair on the third floor.
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Kelly County
You can find a few GTA 6 Magazine Styles for Jason and Lucia in Kelly County. We start things off just outside the Starlet Motel, which becomes your safehouse during chapter 2.
Lucia Magazine Style #1: Lilac Brown 90s Beachy Waves (Hairstyle)
Check the swimming pool in front of Starlet Motel. It’s next to a couple of deck chairs.
Lucia Magazine Style #2: Smoky Blue (Makeup)
Speaking of which, there’s another motel/apartelle with a swimming pool. It’s at the junction of SR-32 and the main thoroughfare in Port Gellhorn.
Jason Magazine Style #1: Platinum Undercut Mullet (Hairstyle)
Go to the northwestern part of Port Gellhorn. You should see a large beachside home, the last one on Ignatius Road just before Wild Hog Point. Go up the steps and head to the other end of the porch.
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Leonard County
There’s only one Magazine Style in Leonard County, and it’s in the subdivision of Bellville.
Magazine Style #1: Diamond-Adorned Pink Cat Eye (Makeup)

If you zoom in on the map, this is the fourth house along the northernmost street in Bellville. Also, if you’re doing Andy’s side missions as Lucia, then the location is just two houses down from where Andy lives.

Something off is going on in this place, though, because there are plenty of, ahem, toys and mannequins lying around. Oh, and there’s also a Jack of Hearts Dancers collectible card in one of the rooms.
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Vice-Dale County: South

Due to the sheer number of GTA 6 Magazine Styles in Vice-Dale County/Vice City, we’ve opted to split up the map into several districts. We start things off with the southern districts of Hamlet, Southside, and Catalan Key.
Lucia Magazine Style #1: Ear Web Buzz Cut (Hairstyle)
Inside a one-storey house in Hamlet. It’s right next to the backyard wrestling encounter against The Gentrifier, which is a rather hilarious Easter egg .
Lucia: Magazine Style #2: Gothic Garnet (Makeup)
Head over to the police station on Palmetto Avenue in Hamlet. Just across the street, you’ll see a warehouse with a red shutter. Enter it and scan the item in the small storage room.
Jason Magazine Style #1: Green & Red Shards Buzz Cut (Hairstyle)

Travel to the shopping complex in the southwestern part of Tequesta--i.e. the one with an Ammu-Nation, clothing store, and sneaker store. You should see an establishment called Mrs. B’s. Follow the metal stairs to the middle section of the buildings.
Jason Magazine Style #2: Light Blonde Wavy Spikes (Hairstyle)
Head to the southern tip of Catalan Key. One of the manors along Ocean Sound Road has a beachside area with a pool. The magazine is on one of the lounging chairs.
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Vice-Dale County: West
Here are the Magazine Styles in Tequesta and Balsero.
Jason Magazine Style #3: Hipster Mustache (Facial Hair)

You can find this GTA 6 Jason Magazine Style by checking the building that’s adjacent to the police station in southern Tequesta. Take the elevator and search for the item on one of the sofas on the roof deck.
Jason Magazine Style #4: Rose Buzz Cut (Hairstyle)
Inside a blue house on NW 26th Street in Balsero. There’s also a collectible card in the bedroom.
Jason Magazine Style #5: Lumberjack (Facial Hair)
Check the sofa in this trailer on NW 22nd Place in Balsero.
Lucia Magazine Style #3: 80s Pop Shimmer (Makeup)
When you’re walking along NW 17th Street in southeast Balsero, look for a green building with the Turnout Warehouse billboard. The scannable object is inside the staff room.
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Vice-Dale County: North
There are more collectibles in Bayside, La Perle, Stockyard, and Decor District.
Lucia Magazine Style #4: Rose High Twin Buns (Hairstyle)

Over at Del Rio Boulevard in northwest La Perle, you’ll see a Drip Drops branch that’s a front for a robbery opportunity. Take out the enemies as you see fit and enter Apartment 05 on the ground floor.
Lucia Magazine Style #5: Tiger Eyes (Makeup)
This GTA 6 Lucia Magazine Style is in the Lot6 bar in Stockyard. The open yard with rental cars is well guarded, so you have to go to the street on the other side of the establishment.
The entrance door is at the building with the “Shake That Thing Hun” mural. As for the magazine, it’s inside the office, which also has a small safe.
Lucia Magazine Style #6: Floral Bun & Wavy Framing (Hairstyle)
NE 6th Avenue is in the southern part of Decor District. Look for a building with a black-and-orange horse mural and open its garage door.
Jason Magazine Style #6: Van Dyke (Facial Hair)
Go to the NOLA branch north of the location where you obtained the Floral Bun hairstyle for Lucia. The item is next to a round limestone sculpture with fountains.
Jason Magazine Style #7: Rainbow Leopard Buzz Cut (Hairstyle)
Check the park on the southern edge of Bayside. The item is on one of the tables where people play chess.
Jason and Lucia Magazine Styles in Vice-Dale County: East
Finally, here are the items in the eastern part of the county--i.e. Ocean Beach, Vice Beach, and Washington Beach.
Jason Magazine Style #8:Blonde-Brown Side Part Curtains (Hairstyle)

Make your way to Thompson Avenue in Vice Beach and look for the Taco Jonudo restaurant. Right beside that, you’ll see a sign for The Emerald. Enter the establishment--which is actually a gathering spot for swingers and nudists--and take the elevator to the rooftop. The magazine is at the other end of the pool near the deck chairs.
Lucia Magazine Style #7: Orange-Purple Neon Cat Eye (Makeup)

Travel to Lux Apollo Heights in southwest Ocean Beach. This hotel has two sets of elevators that lead to two different penthouse suites. One of them has a scannable magazine, and the other has a collectible card. Anyway, the magazine itself is on the counter beside the stove.
Lucia Magazine Style #8: Spiky Bun & Framing (Hairstyle)

This GTA 6 Lucia Magazine Style is a bit hard to find, but it’s in Annabelle Hotel & Suites. Almost all doors are locked, but there’s actually a vendor entrance along Thompson Avenue to the southwest. Use it to gain entry, then ride the elevator to the rooftop. From there, look for the magazine on a wooden counter near a jacuzzi.
Lucia Magazine Style #9: Pixie Cut (Hairstyle)
This item is in a hotel along Shorebeach Road. Take the elevator to the rooftop and circle around to the opposite side until you see a terrace below you with a pool.

These are the GTA 6 Magazine Styles for Jason and Lucia. Once you’ve obtained all of them, you’ll have more options when changing the looks of your characters. If you’re interested about other customization cosmetics, feel free to visit our Magazine Tattoos guide and Luxury Watches guide .

You’re going to feel lost as you explore the cities, beachfronts, and seedy underbelly of Leonida. If you need more help navigating the massive game world and tackling its activities, be sure to check our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub .

articles.headline: Denis Villeneuve Wishes ‘Dune: Part Three’ Had Its Own Weekend
keyFacts: Director Denis Villeneuve told Time Magazine he is deeply disappointed that Dune: Part Three shares its December 18 release date with Avengers: Doomsday.
Warner Bros. locked down the December 18, 2026 release date for Dune first in June 2024 before Marvel scheduled Avengers for the same day.
Villeneuve stated he has accepted his fate and hopes his threequel can survive the shared weekend, which some speculate could be a massive box office event.
body: In less than a month,Â Dune: Part ThreeÂ will share the silver screen withÂ Avengers: Doomsday. For the blockbuster-minded, this shared date has been nicknamed “Dunesday” (a la “Barbenheimer”), and many excited viewers plan to see both in one day.

You know who’s not jazzed about this? Denis Villeneuve, who told Time Magazine that he was “deeply disappointed” to share December 18 with Marvel’s latest superhero outing. Compared toÂ Avengers,Â he considersÂ DuneÂ a “sexy little animal [with] a lot of firepower” that couldn’t move its date due to IMAX. With two heavy hitters sharing a single weekend, he’s “accepted my fate” and just hopes his threequel can “survive” the experience.

To Villeneuve’s point, Dune: Part ThreeÂ had December 18, 2026 first when WB locked it down back in June 2024. Marvel later putÂ DoomsdayÂ on that date in May 2025, back when it was initially meant for that month and still The Kang Dynasty. Before either movie got a full trailer, there was speculation on wheter one of them would step down, which didn’t happen. As is, Villeneuve’s confident his film has the goods and DunesdayÂ could have “one of the biggest box office weekends of all time,” if all goes well.

Sure, they’re both major movies, but you have to feel for Villeneuve a bit. He was initially hopeful that Part Three could have an easy release compared to the first two Dune movies’ having bad luck. (If you forgot, they were impacted respectively by the early pandemic days and Hollywood strikes.) Sharing with an AvengersÂ movie may be the worst problem to have, and Dune has managed to hit big with audiences. But the holiday movie season is packed, and some might make time for just one movie to start with. How many will start withÂ Dune?
